You are sandy_walnut42, one of 10 agents working together on the same task on a shared platform. All
agents form one swarm, organized into groups. You are in group_1 with gentle_otter27, pale_lantern48, urban_comet97, zesty_lantern63. Each agent works in
its own sandbox, on its own git repository. Your group also shares one `main` branch, which every member
can push to. Your group has a private channel (`group`) that only its members can see and post in. All
10 agents, in every group, can read and post in the public channel (`public`). Work together with
your teammates to make your group's `main` as good as possible. Use `group` to coordinate within your
group, and `public` to share general findings with other groups.

## Setting
Your task is to recreate a program from scratch based only on its observable behavior and bundled documentation.
You are given a reference executable and its documentation.
Treat the reference executable as a specification you can query through its normal user interface.

Your submission must be an independent implementation.
Using the original source code, wrapping the reference executable, or installing an existing implementation does not satisfy the task and will receive no credit.
It will be detected by an automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.

<RULES>
## What is NOT allowed

### 1. Using an existing implementation

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the reference executable

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The reference `/opt/reference/executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the reference executable (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that only runs `chmod +x ./executable` or copies the reference executable (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. How the reference executable may be observed

All information about the reference `/opt/reference/executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `/opt/reference/executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `/opt/reference/executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the reference `/opt/reference/executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

## Your repository and your group's main
- In your sandbox, `/workspace` is your own git repository, and the reference executable is in `/opt/reference`. No one else can see it.
- Your group's shared `main` is the remote `team`. Fetch it with `git fetch team` (you get `team/main`),
  and push to it with `git push team HEAD:main`. **Your local files do not update automatically when a
  teammate pushes.**
- A push must be a fast-forward: if `main` has moved since you last fetched, the push is rejected. Fetch,
  merge `team/main` into your work, and push again.
- When you push, the platform posts in `group` on your behalf, with your commit message, a summary of the
  changed files, and a pointer to the new `main`. Write commit messages that say what changed.
- Other groups cannot see your group's `main`.
- Your git name and email are preconfigured as your agent name. Do not change them.
- Commit with `git commit -m "<message>"`: there is no editor in the sandbox, so a commit without `-m`
  fails with an empty message.
- Run the reference executable and your experiments outside `/workspace` (for example in `/tmp`), so that they do not change your
  repository.

## Scoring rule
Your payoff is the swarm's score on this task: the highest score among all groups, where a group's score
is the fraction of hidden tests passed by the code on its `main` at the end. Every agent receives the
same payoff.
- **Only the code on your group's `main` at the end is graded.** Code in your own repository, or shared
  through pointers, does not count until it is pushed to `main`. If no one pushes, the initial commit is
  graded.
- Everyone keeps working until time runs out.

## Platform
The platform is the shared place where agents post and ask each other questions. In `group`, announce
what you are exploring, building, or have found: a direction you are exploring, a component you are
building, a proposal for how to organize your group's work, or a question. In `public`, share general
findings (how the original program behaves in some case, a useful test command, a tricky edge case) with the other groups.
- `post` publishes a message to `group` or `public`, with a title: a one-line summary of the message, up
  to 120 characters. Every post gets a number. Mention someone with @name.
- To share code, commit it, then list it in the post's `attach`. The platform adds a pointer
  (`[[<sha>:<path>#La-b]]`) to the post for each item. `attach` can name:
  - `path#La-b`: a file in your `HEAD`, optionally with a line range;
  - `<sha>:path#La-b`: a file in another commit;
  - a commit's sha, or `HEAD`: a whole commit;
  - `file:<path>#La-b`: the current content of a single file, even if it is not committed. Readers see
    only that file.
  Pointing at a commit makes all files in that commit readable. Uncommitted changes are not shared.
- Who can read a pointer depends on the channel: in `group`, only your group; in `public`, every agent.
- `read_feed` lists the new posts in `group`, the latest 20 posts in `public`, and any
  unopened posts that mention you, one line each (number, author, channel, title). `read_feed` with a
  post's number shows its full text, with its pointers expanded into the code and a diff against your own
  version.
- You can fetch any code shared with you into your repository with `git fetch origin` (as
  `origin/shared/<author>/<sha>`), and then merge or cherry-pick what you want.

After each action, a platform notice lists the new posts on the channels you can read, one line each (number,
author, channel, title, and a marker when the post carries code). A post that mentions you appears in
every notice until you open it with `read_feed` and its number.

## Working together
- Start by **getting an overview of what the reference program supports**, enough to understand how the
  program should behave in its main cases, and share it in `group` as a list (if a teammate has
  already posted one, add to theirs), so the group can keep extending the plan and everyone stays up
  to date on which areas are covered. Then **agree with your teammates on how to work together**:
  split the work, or have several members build the same part and compare, keeping the best of each.
  If parts depend on each other, agree on the interfaces first, and while you wait for a part you
  need, write tests for it with expected output from the reference program.
- If a teammate has already posted a plan, **follow it and propose changes to it** instead of posting
  a competing one.
- Work in a cycle: (1) pick an area and say so in `group`; (2) build it on top of the latest `main`;
  (3) compare its output with the reference program on the same inputs; (4) commit, `git fetch team`, merge
  `team/main`, and `git push team HEAD:main`; (5) post what you finished in `group`, with a pointer,
  then go back to (1). Report a part as done only once it is on `main`: a part that is not on `main`
  does not count.
- Passing your own tests does not mean the task is done: always assume the hidden tests cover more
  than your tests do. **When your tests all pass, test more areas.** Add cases for features and
  options your tests do not cover yet, including the parts your teammates are handling. A new area
  usually matters more than more cases in an area that already works.
- **Never stop calling tool before time is up. When you are not sure what to do next, review the
  whole program on `main` again** as a reviewer looking for bugs: features of the reference program that
  are missing or only partly handled, edge cases (empty input, `null`, deep nesting, large numbers,
  unusual option combinations), and error paths. Do not review only your own part: test the whole
  program, including your teammates' parts, with inputs you have not tried yet. Test each suspicion
  against the reference program, and fix what differs.
- **If one approach keeps failing, change the approach instead of retrying it.** Post in `group` what
  you tried, so teammates do not repeat it and can suggest other ideas. If you are still stuck, put a
  version that handles the common cases on `main` for now, and come back to it later.
- Do not leave hard parts as known gaps. Come back to them, discuss them with your teammates, and solve
  as many of them as possible: **keep improving `main` until time runs out.**

## Working with agents from other groups
- **Each group must have its own complete and runnable version of the program on its `main`.**
- `public` is a channel where you share general findings with the other groups: how the reference program
  behaves (how the original program behaves in some case, a useful test command, a tricky edge case), edge cases worth testing, approaches that worked or did not, and code that
  others may find useful. Post what you learned that other groups are likely to miss. Keep the
  coordination of your own group's work in `group`.
- Read what others post in `public`. When a finding would improve your group's version, use it in your
  own code and test it against the reference program. Shared code is there to show how something can be
  done: take the idea or the fix you need.

## Task context

The executable is located at `/opt/reference/executable`.
You also have access to the existing documentation.

## Your task
Implement a program whose externally observable behavior matches the reference executable.
Write it in **Python 3.10**.
- Its documentation is in `/workspace` (README and other files). There is no source code and no internet.
- Write your implementation in your own workspace `/workspace`, starting from `/workspace/main.py`.
  You may add more Python modules next to it. **Standard library only.**
- `/workspace/compile.sh` is already provided: at evaluation time it turns `main.py` into the program under
  test. **Do not run it in your workspace.** Test your code with `python3 main.py ...`.
- Your implementation is scored on hidden tests that compare its behavior against the original.

**Recommended workflow:** read the documentation, run the original program to learn its behavior, then write
the code. Start writing `main.py` early and grow it incrementally: an incomplete implementation that
handles the common cases scores far better than none. After each change, run your code against the
original to check it. If an approach keeps failing, step back and consider other causes before trying

Static analysis for GitHub Actions

Usage: executable [OPTIONS] <INPUT>...

Input Options:
  <INPUT>...
          The inputs to audit.
          
          These can be individual workflow filenames, action definitions (typically `action.yml`), entire directories, or a `user/repo` slug for a GitHub repository. In the latter case, a `@ref` can be appended to audit the repository at a particular git reference state.
          
          Use `-` to read a single input from stdin.

      --collect <KIND>...
          Control which kinds of inputs are collected for auditing.
          
          By default, all workflows and composite actions are collected, while honoring `.gitignore` files.

          Possible values:
          - all:        Collect all possible inputs, ignoring `.gitignore` files
          - default:    Collect all possible inputs, respecting `.gitignore` files
          - workflows:  Collect workflows
          - actions:    Collect action definitions (i.e. `action.yml`)
          - dependabot: Collect Dependabot configuration files (i.e. `dependabot.yml`)
          
          [default: default]

      --strict-collection
          Fail instead of warning on syntax and schema errors in collected inputs

Audit Options:
      --fix[=<MODE>]
          Fix findings automatically, when available (EXPERIMENTAL)

          Possible values:
          - safe:        Apply only safe fixes (the default)
          - unsafe-only: Apply only unsafe fixes
          - all:         Apply all fixes, both safe and unsafe

  -p, --pedantic
          Emit 'pedantic' findings.
          
          This is an alias for --persona=pedantic.

      --persona <PERSONA>
          The persona to use while auditing

          Possible values:
          - auditor:  The "auditor" persona (false positives OK)
          - pedantic: The "pedantic" persona (code smells OK)
          - regular:  The "regular" persona (minimal false positives)
          
          [default: regular]

      --min-severity <LEVEL>
          Filter all results below this severity
          
          [possible values: informational, low, medium, high]

      --min-confidence <LEVEL>
          Filter all results below this confidence
          
          [possible values: low, medium, high]

      --no-ignores
          Don't honor ignore comments or ignore rules in configuration

Output Options:
  -v, --verbose...
          Increase logging verbosity

  -q, --quiet...
          Decrease logging verbosity

      --format <KIND>
          The output format to emit. By default, cargo-style diagnostics will be emitted

          Possible values:
          - plain:   cargo-style output
          - json:    JSON-formatted output (currently v1)
          - json-v1: "v1" JSON format
          - sarif:   SARIF-formatted output
          - github:  GitHub Actions workflow command-formatted output
          
          [default: plain]

      --no-progress
          Don't show progress bars, even if the terminal supports them

      --color <WHEN>
          Control the use of color in output

          Possible values:
          - auto:   Use color output if the output supports it
          - always: Force color output, even if the output isn't a terminal
          - never:  Disable color output, even if the output is a compatible terminal

      --render-links <WHEN>
          Whether to render OSC 8 links in the output.
          
          This affects links under audit IDs, as well as any links produced by audit rules.
          
          Only affects `--format=plain` (the default).

          Possible values:
          - auto:   Render OSC 8 links in output if support is detected
          - always: Always render OSC 8 links in output
          - never:  Never render OSC 8 links in output
          
          [env: ZIZMOR_RENDER_LINKS=]
          [default: auto]

      --show-audit-urls <WHEN>
          Whether to render audit URLs in the output, separately from any URLs embedded in OSC 8 links.
          
          Only affects `--format=plain` (the default).

          Possible values:
          - auto:   Render audit URLs in output automatically based on output format and runtime context
          - always: Always render audit URLs in output
          - never:  Never render audit URLs in output
          
          [env: ZIZMOR_SHOW_AUDIT_URLS=]
          [default: auto]

      --no-exit-codes
          Disable all error codes besides success and tool failure

Network Options:
  -o, --offline
          Perform only offline operations.
          
          This disables all online audit rules, and prevents zizmor from auditing remote repositories.
          
          [env: ZIZMOR_OFFLINE=]

      --gh-token <GH_TOKEN>
          The GitHub API token to use [env: GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN or ZIZMOR_GITHUB_TOKEN]

      --gh-hostname <GH_HOSTNAME>
          The GitHub Server Hostname. Defaults to github.com
          
          [env: GH_HOST=]
          [default: github.com]

      --no-online-audits
          Perform only offline audits.
          
          This is a weaker version of `--offline`: instead of completely forbidding all online operations, it only disables audits that require connectivity.
          
          [env: ZIZMOR_NO_ONLINE_AUDITS=]

      --cache-dir <DIR>
          The directory to use for HTTP caching. By default, a host-appropriate user-caching directory will be used

Options:
      --lsp
          Run in language server mode (EXPERIMENTAL).
          
          This flag cannot be used with any other flags.

  -c, --config <FILE>
          The configuration file to load. This loads a single configuration file across all input groups, which may not be what you intend
          
          [env: ZIZMOR_CONFIG=]

      --no-config
          Disable all configuration loading

      --completions <SHELL>
          Generate tab completion scripts for the specified shell

          Possible values:
          - bash:       Bourne Again `SHell` (bash)
          - elvish:     Elvish shell
          - fish:       Friendly Interactive `SHell` (fish)
          - nushell:    Nushell

There are four input sources that `zizmor` knows about: 1. Individual workflow and action files, e.g. `foo.yml` and `my-action/action.yml`; 2. "Local" GitHub repositories in the form of a directory, e.g. `my-repo/`; 3. "Remote" GitHub repositories in the form of a "slug", e.g. `pypa/sampleproject`; !!! tip By default, a remote repository will be audited from the `HEAD` of the default branch. To control this, you can append a `git` reference to the slug: ```bash # audit at HEAD on the default branch zizmor example/example # audit at branch or tag `v1` zizmor example/example@v1 # audit at a specific SHA zizmor example/example@abababab... ``` !!! tip Remote auditing requires Internet access and a GitHub API token. See [Operating Modes](#operating-modes) and [GitHub API token permissions](#github-api-token-permissions) for more information. 4. Standard input, via `-`. !!! tip Support for auditing from standard input is available in `v1.24.0` and later. ```bash # pipe a workflow from stdin cat workflow.yml | zizmor - # or use a heredoc zizmor - <<'EOF' on: push jobs: test: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v3 EOF ``` When reading from stdin, `zizmor` automatically infers the input type (workflow, action, or Dependabot config). !!! note `-` cannot be combined with other inputs, and `--fix` is not supported with stdin input. `zizmor` can audit multiple inputs in the same run, and different input sources can be mixed and matched: ```bash # audit a single local workflow, an entire local directory, and # a remote repository all in the same run zizmor ../example.yml ../other-repo/ example/example ``` When auditing local directories and/or remote repositories, `zizmor` will collect all known input kinds by default. To configure collection behavior, you can use the `--collect=...` option. ```bash # collect everything regardless of `.gitignore` patterns zizmor --collect=all example/example # collect everything while respecting `.gitignore` patterns (the default) zizmor --collect=default example/example # collect only workflows zizmor --collect=workflows example/example # collect only actions zizmor --collect=actions example/example # collect only Dependabot configs zizmor --collect=dependabot example/example # collect only workflows and actions (not Dependabot configs) zizmor --collect=workflows,actions example/example ``` !!! warning "Deprecation" `--collect=workflows-only` and `--collect=actions-only` are deprecated aliases for `--collect=workflows` and `--collect=actions`, respectively, as of `v1.15.0`. Users should switch to the non-deprecated forms, as the deprecated forms will be removed in a future release. !!! tip `--collect=all` can be significantly slower than `--collect=default`, particularly when collecting from directories that contain large hierarchies of paths that would be ignored by `.gitignore` patterns. !!! tip `--collect=...` only controls input collection from repository input sources. In other words, `zizmor --collect=actions workflow.yml` *will* audit `workflow.yml`, since it was passed explicitly and not collected indirectly. By default, `zizmor` will warn (but not fail) if it fails to parse an input file. To turn these warnings into failures, you can use the `--strict-collection` option: ```bash # fail if any files collected from example/example fail to parse zizmor --strict-collection example/example ``` !!! important `--strict-collection` is available in `v1.7.0` and later. ## Operating Modes `zizmor` has three *operating modes*: * **Offline**: `zizmor` will not access the Internet, will not fetch remote repositories, and will not perform any audits that require online access (e.g. to the GitHub API). * **Online**: `zizmor` will fetch remote repositories as necessary, and will perform all audits that require online access. * **Online sans audits**: `zizmor` will fetch remote repositories as necessary, but will skip any audits that require online access. `zizmor` attempts to select a default operating mode based on the user's environment: - If `ZIZMOR_OFFLINE` is set, then `zizmor` runs in offline mode. - If `GH_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN` or `ZIZMOR_GITHUB_TOKEN` is set, then `zizmor` runs in online mode with audits. - Additionally `ZIZMOR_NO_ONLINE_AUDITS` is set, then `zizmor` runs online sans audits. - If neither `ZIZMOR_OFFLINE` nor `GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN`/`ZIZMOR_GITHUB_TOKEN` are set, then `zizmor` runs in offline mode. Or, as a flowchart: ```mermaid flowchart TD B{ZIZMOR_OFFLINE set?} -- Yes --> C[Offline mode] B -- No --> D{GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN/ZIZMOR_GITHUB_TOKEN set?} D -- No --> C D -- Yes --> E{ZIZMOR_NO_ONLINE_AUDITS set?} E -- Yes --> F[Online sans audits mode] E -- No --> G[Online mode] ``` Each operating mode can also be made explicit through command-line flags: ```bash # force offline, even if GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN/ZIZMOR_GITHUB_TOKEN is present # this disables all online actions, including repository fetches zizmor --offline workflow.yml # passing a token explicitly will enable online mode # in this case, we use the `gh` CLI token zizmor --gh-token $(gh auth token) workflow.yml # online for the purpose of fetching the input (example/example), # but all audits themselves are offline zizmor --no-online-audits --gh-token $(gh auth token) example/example ``` ### GitHub API token permissions !!! tip If you're running `zizmor` locally with an online mode, it is **strongly recommended** that you use `gh auth token` from the [GitHub CLI] to automatically access an API token and avoid error-prone manual provisioning. This token is almost always pre-configured with sufficient permissions, meaning that you **do not** need any of the manual steps below. [GitHub CLI]: https://cli.github.com/ When running in an online mode, `zizmor` uses the GitHub API for various operations, including fetching a repository's contents (for the collection phase) and fetching tag/branch/commit histories (for the auditing phase). Generally speaking, `zizmor` does **not** require any special permissions from its GitHub API token: it uses the token *primarily* to provide authentication for rate-limited API requests. However, if you are auditing a private remote repository (e.g. `zizmor myorg/private-repo`) or auditing _any_ input that contains private references (e.g. `#!yaml uses: myorg/private-action`), then you may need to provision permissions for the token: - `#!yaml contents: read` for GitHub Actions - `repo` for OAuth tokens and "classic" PATs - An appropriate repository access scope for fine-grained PATs In addition to these permissions, some integrations of `zizmor` (like GitHub Advanced Security) may require additional permissions in the context of GitHub Actions. See [Integration - GitHub Actions](./integrations.md#github-actions) for more details. ## Output formats `zizmor` always produces output on `stdout`. ### Cargo-style output ("plain") By default, `zizmor` produces `cargo`-style diagnostic output. ```console error[template-injection]: code injection via template expansion --> ./tests/integration/test-data/template-injection/pr-425-backstop/action.yml:31:56 | 29 | uses: azure/powershell@whatever | ------------…5433 tokens truncated… never executes any code, nor does it have access to any runtime state. In contrast, GitHub Actions workflow and action definitions are highly dynamic, and can be influenced by inputs that can only be inspected at runtime. For example, here is a workflow where a job's matrix is generated at runtime by a previous job, making the matrix impossible to analyze statically: ```yaml build-matrix: name: Build the matrix runs-on: ubuntu-latest outputs: matrix: ${{ steps.set-matrix.outputs.matrix }} steps: - id: set-matrix run: | echo "matrix=$(python generate_matrix.py)" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}" run: name: ${{ matrix.name }} needs: - build-matrix runs-on: ubuntu-latest strategy: matrix: ${{ fromJson(needs.build-matrix.outputs.matrix) }} steps: - run: | echo "hello ${{ matrix.something }}" ``` In the above, the expansion of `${{ matrix.something }}` is entirely controlled by the output of `generate_matrix.py`, which is only known at runtime. In such cases, `zizmor` will err on the side of verbosity. For example, the [template-injection](./audits.md#template-injection) audit will flag `${{ matrix.something }}` as a potential code injection risk, since it can't infer anything about what `matrix.something` might expand to. ### `zizmor` audits workflow and action _definitions_ only { #definitions-only } `zizmor` audits workflow and action _definitions_ only. That means the contents of `foo.yml` (for your workflow definitions) or `action.yml` (for your composite or Docker action definitions). In practice, this means that `zizmor` does **not** analyze other files referenced by workflow and action definitions. For example: ```yaml example: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - name: step-1 run: | echo foo=$(bar) >> $GITHUB_ENV - name: step-2 run: | # some-script.sh contains the same code as step-1 ./some-script.sh ``` `zizmor` can analyze `step-1` above, because the code it executes is present within the workflow definition itself. It *cannot* analyze `step-2` beyond the presence of a script execution, since it doesn't audit shell scripts or any other kind of files. More generally, `zizmor` cannot analyze files indirectly referenced within workflow/action definitions, as they may not actually exist until runtime. For example, `some-script.sh` above may have been generated or downloaded outside of any repository-tracked state. ### YAML anchors { #yaml-anchors } !!! warning "Beta" `zizmor`'s support for YAML anchors is currently in **beta**. If you encounter a problem, please [file a bug report](https://github.com/zizmorcore/zizmor/issues/new). `zizmor` tries very hard to present *useful* source spans in its audit results. To do this, `zizmor` needs to know a lot of about the inner workings of the YAML serialization format that GitHub Actions workflows, action definitions, and Dependabot files are expressed in. YAML is a complicated serialization format, but GitHub *mostly* uses a tractable subset of it. One conspicuous exception to this is [YAML anchors](https://yaml.org/spec/1.2.2/#3222-anchors-and-aliases), which GitHub has [decided to support](https://github.blog/changelog/2025-09-18-actions-yaml-anchors-and-non-public-workflow-templates/) in workflow and action definitions as of September 2025. Anchors make `zizmor`'s analysis job *much* harder, as they introduce a layer of (arbitrarily deep) indirection and misalignment between the deserialized object model (which is what `zizmor` analyzes) and the source representation (which `zizmor` spans back to). If you're having issues with inputs containing anchors, see [Troubleshooting - YAML anchors]. [Troubleshooting - YAML anchors]: ./troubleshooting.md#yaml-anchors --- description: zizmor's configuration file and configurable behaviors. --- # Configuration !!! note Configuration support was added in `v0.2.0`. `zizmor` supports a small amount of configuration via [YAML] config files, typically named `zizmor.yml` or `zizmor.yaml`. [YAML]: https://learnxinyminutes.com/docs/yaml/ ## Discovery !!! note Configuration is *always* optional, and can always be skipped with `--no-config`. If `--no-config` is passed, no configuration is ever loaded. !!! tip `zizmor`'s configuration discovery behavior changed significantly in `v1.13.0`. See the [release notes](./release-notes.md) for details. `zizmor` discovers configuration files in two conceptually distinct ways: 1. **Global** discovery: when explicitly given a configuration file via `--config` or `ZIZMOR_CONFIG`, that file is used for **all** inputs. In other words: when a global configuration file is used no other configuration files are discovered or loaded, even if they're present according to the local discovery rules below. 2. **Local** discovery: when no global configuration file is given, `zizmor` looks for configuration files _for each given input_. The rules for this discovery are as follows: - File inputs (e.g. `zizmor path/to/workflow.yml`): `zizmor` performs directory discovery starting in the directory containing the given file. - Directory inputs (e.g. `zizmor .`): `zizmor` looks for a `zizmor.yml` or `zizmor.yaml` file in the given directory, the `.github` child directory, or any parent, up to the filesystem root or the first `.git` directory. !!! example Given an invocation like `zizmor ./repo/`, `zizmor` will attempt to discover configuration files in the following order: 1. `./repo/.github/zizmor.yml` 2. `./repo/.github/zizmor.yaml` 3. `./repo/zizmor.yml` 4. `./repo/zizmor.yaml` 5. `./repo/../.github/zizmor.yml` 6. `./repo/../.github/zizmor.yaml` 7. ...and so on, until the filesystem root or a `.git/` directory is found. !!! note `zizmor .github/workflows/` is a special case: in this case, discovery starts in `.github/`, the parent of the given directory. This is done to avoid confusion between a `zizmor.yml` config file and a `zizmor.yml` workflow file. - Remote repository inputs (e.g. `zizmor owner/repo`): `zizmor` looks for a `zizmor.yml` or `.github/zizmor.yml` in the root of the repository. In general, **most users will want to use local discovery**, which is the default behavior. Global discovery only takes precedence when explicitly requested with `--config` or `ZIZMOR_CONFIG`. ## Settings ### `rules..disable` {#rules-id-disable} _Type_: `boolean` Disables the audit entirely if `true`. !!! important `rules..disable` was added in `v1.13.0`. !!! warning For most users, disabling audits should be a **measure of last resort**. Disabled rules don't show up in ignored or suppressed finding counts, making it **very easy** to accidentally miss important new findings. Before disabling an audit entirely, consider one of the following alternatives: 1. Ignoring specific findings via [`rules..ignore`](#rulesidignore). 1. Changing your [persona](./usage.md#using-personas) to a less sensitive one. For example, consider removing `--persona=pedantic` or `--persona=auditor` if you're using one of those. When set, inputs covered by this configuration file will not be analyzed by the given audit. For example, here is a configuration file that disables the [`template-injection`](./audits.md#template-injection) audit: ```yaml title="zizmor.yml" rules: template-injection: disable: true ``` Multiple audits can be disabled as well: ```yaml title="zizmor.yml" rules: template-injection: disable: true unpinned-uses: disable: true ``` ### `rules..ignore` {#rules-id-ignore} _Type_: `array` Per-audit ignore rules. Each member of `rules..ignore` is a _workflow rule_, formatted as follows: ``` filename.yml[:line[:column]] ``` where `filename.yml` is the base filename of the workflow, and `line` and `column` are both optional 1-based values indicating the exact line-and-column location to ignore. If one or both are absent, then the rule applies to the entire file or entire line. !!! important Composite action findings cannot be ignored via `zizmor.yml` currently, They can be ignored inline [with comments](./usage.md#ignoring-results). For example, here is a configuration file with two different audit ignore rule groups: ```yaml title="zizmor.yml" rules: template-injection: ignore: # ignore line 100 in ci.yml, any column - ci.yml:100 # ignore all lines and columns in tests.yml - tests.yml use-trusted-publishing: ignore: # ignore line 12, column 10 on pypi.yml - pypi.yml:12:10 ``` ### `rules..config` {#rules-id-config} _Type_: `object` Per-audit configuration, where `id` is the audit's name, e.g. [`unpinned-uses`](./audits.md#unpinned-uses). Not all audits are configurable. See each audit's documentation for details. ### `rules..remap` {#rules-id-remap} _Type_: `object` Remap parts of the rule. Currently, only severity is supported. !!! note Remappings are applied in a blanket fashion. For example, if you remap an audit's severity to `high`, both `medium` _and_ `low` findings will be re-graded as `high`. #### `rules..remap.severity` {#rules-id-remap-severity} !!! important `rules..remap.severity` was added in `v1.25.0`. For example, here is a configuration file with the rule severity remapped: ```yaml title="zizmor.yml" rules: artipacked: remap: severity: high # one of: informational, low, medium, high ``` ## Patterns Several audits support being configured with _patterns_, which can be used to match things like `#!yaml uses:` clauses. These patterns share common syntaxes, and are described here. ### Repository patterns Repository patterns are used to match `#!yaml uses:` clauses. The following patterns are supported, in order of specificity: - `owner/repo/subpath@ref`: matches the exact repository, including subpath (if given) and ref. The subpath is optional. !!! example `github/codeql-action/init@v2` matches `#!yaml uses: github/codeql-action/init@v2`, but **not** `#!yaml uses: github/codeql-action/init@main`. - `owner/repo/subpath`: match all `#!yaml uses:` clauses that are **exact** matches for the `owner/repo/subpath` pattern. The `subpath` can be an arbitrarily deep subpath, but is not optional. Any ref is matched. !!! example `github/codeql-action/init` matches `#!yaml uses: github/codeql-action/init@v2`, but **not** `#!yaml uses: github/codeql-action@v2`. - `owner/repo`: match all `#!yaml uses:` clauses that are **exact** matches for the `owner/repo` pattern. Any ref is matched. !!! example `actions/cache` matches `#!yaml uses: actions/cache@v3`, but **not** `#!yaml uses: actions/cache/save@v3` or `#!yaml uses: actions/cache/restore@v3`. - `owner/repo/*`: match all `#!yaml uses:` clauses that come from the given `owner/repo`. Any subpath or ref is matched. !!! example `github/codeql-action/*` matches `#!yaml uses: github/codeql-action/init@v2`, `#!yaml uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v2`, and `#!yaml uses: github/codeql-action@v2` itself. - `owner/*`: match all `#!yaml uses:` clauses that have the given `owner`. Any repo, subpath, or ref is matched. !!! example `actions/*` matches both `#!yaml uses: actions/checkout@v4` and `#!yaml uses: actions/setup-node@v4`, but **not** `#!yaml uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1`. - `*`: match all `#!yaml uses:` clauses. !!! example `*` matches `#!yaml uses: actions/checkout` and `#!yaml uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1`.

const patch = "*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /workspace/collector.py
+"""Local input discovery for the zizmor-compatible command line."""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import fnmatch
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+import re
+import sys
+
+KINDS = {"all", "default", "workflows", "actions", "dependabot"}
+
+
+def infer_kind(path: str, content: str = "") -> str:
+    name = Path(path).name.lower()
+    if name in ("dependabot.yml", "dependabot.yaml") or re.search(r"(?m)^\s*package-ecosystem\s*:", content):
+        return "dependabot"
+    if name in ("action.yml", "action.yaml") or re.search(r"(?m)^\s*runs\s*:\s*\n", content):
+        return "actions"
+    return "workflows"
+
+
+def _ignored(path: Path, root: Path) -> bool:
+    """Apply the common .gitignore forms encountered during input collection."""
+    try:
+        rel = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()
+    except ValueError:
+        return False
+    directory = path.parent
+    patterns = []
+    while True:
+        ignore_file = directory / ".gitignore"
+        if ignore_file.is_file():
+            for line in ignore_file.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines():
+                line = line.strip()
+                if line and not line.startswith("#"):
+                    patterns.append((directory, line))
+        if directory == root or directory.parent == directory:
+            break
+        directory = directory.parent
+    ignored = False
+    for base, pattern in patterns:
+        negated = pattern.startswith("!")
+        if negated:
+            pattern = pattern[1:]
+        target = path.relative_to(base).as_posix() if path.is_relative_to(base) else rel
+        pat = pattern.lstrip("/")
+        match = fnmatch.fnmatchcase(target, pat) or ("/" not in pat and any(fnmatch.fnmatchcase(p, pat) for p in target.split("/")))
+        if match:
+            ignored = not negated
+    return ignored
+
+
+def collect(inputs, collect="default", stdin_text=None):
+    """Return input records {path, content, kind}; explicit files are always included.
+
+    `collect` accepts comma-separated kinds or a sequence. Stdin is represented by '-'.
+    """
+    if isinstance(collect, str):
+        kinds = set(x for x in collect.split(",") if x)
+    else:
+        kinds = set(collect)
+    if not kinds:
+        kinds = {"default"}
+    kinds = {"workflows" if x == "workflows-only" else "actions" if x == "actions-only" else x for x in kinds}
+    if not kinds <= KINDS:
+        raise ValueError("invalid collection kind")
+    args = list(inputs)
+    if "-" in args:
+        if len(args) != 1:
+            raise ValueError("stdin cannot be combined with other inputs")
+        data = sys.stdin.read() if stdin_text is None else stdin_text
+        return [{"path": "<stdin>", "content": data, "kind": infer_kind("", data)}]
+    records, seen = [], set()
+
+    def add(file, explicit=False):
+        p = Path(file)
+        try:
+            if not p.is_file():
+                return
+            data = p.read_text(errors="replace")
+        except (OSError, UnicodeError):
+            return
+        kind = infer_kind(str(p), data)
+        if explicit or "all" in kinds or "default" in kinds or kind in kinds:
+            key = str(p)
+            if key not in seen:
+                seen.add(key)
+                records.append({"path": key, "content": data, "kind": kind})
+
+    for arg in args:
+        p = Path(arg)
+        if p.is_file():
+            add(p, True)
+        elif p.is_dir():
+            root = p.resolve()
+            for current, dirs, files in os.walk(root):
+                cur = Path(current)
+                if ".git" in dirs:
+                    dirs.remove(".git")
+                if "default" not in kinds and "all" not in kinds:
+                    dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if d not in {".git", "node_modules", "vendor"}]
+                else:
+                    dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if d != ".git"]
+                for name in files:
+                    f = cur / name
+                    if name.lower() not in {"action.yml", "action.yaml", "dependabot.yml", "dependabot.yaml"} and not ("workflows" in f.parts and f.suffix.lower() in {".yml", ".yaml"}):
+                        continue
+                    if "all" not in kinds and "default" not in kinds and infer_kind(str(f)) not in kinds:
+                        continue
+                    if "all" not in kinds and _ignored(f, root):
+                        continue
+                    add(f)
+        else:
+            # Remote repository slugs require network collection; preserve a useful diagnostic record upstream.
+            continue
+    return records
+
*** End Patch";
text(await tools.apply_patch(patch));

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""A small offline-compatible zizmor command line implementation."""
import argparse
import os
import re
import sys
from collector import collect
from audit import audit_text
from audit_extra import auditor_findings, concurrency_findings, pedantic_permission_findings
from output import render
from cli import handle_special
from ignores import filter_inline_ignores
from configuration import discover_config, apply_config


def parser():
    p=argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="executable", description="Static analysis for GitHub Actions")
    p.add_argument("inputs", nargs="*")
    p.add_argument("--collect", action="append", default=[])
    p.add_argument("--strict-collection", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("--fix", nargs="?", const="safe", choices=["safe","unsafe-only","all"])
    p.add_argument("-p","--pedantic", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("--persona", choices=["auditor","pedantic","regular"], default="regular")
    p.add_argument("--min-severity", choices=["informational","low","medium","high"])
    p.add_argument("--min-confidence", choices=["low","medium","high"])
    p.add_argument("--no-ignores", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("-v","--verbose", action="count", default=0)
    p.add_argument("-q","--quiet", action="count", default=0)
    p.add_argument("--format", choices=["plain","json","json-v1","sarif","github"], default="plain")
    p.add_argument("--no-progress", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("--color", choices=["auto","always","never"], default="auto")
    p.add_argument("--render-links", choices=["auto","always","never"], default="auto")
    p.add_argument("--show-audit-urls", choices=["auto","always","never"], default="auto")
    p.add_argument("--no-exit-codes", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("-o","--offline", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("--gh-token")
    p.add_argument("--gh-hostname", default=os.environ.get("GH_HOST","github.com"))
    p.add_argument("--no-online-audits", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("--cache-dir")
    p.add_argument("--lsp", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("-c","--config", default=os.environ.get("ZIZMOR_CONFIG"))
    p.add_argument("--no-config", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("--completions", choices=["bash","elvish","fish","nushell","powershell","zsh"])
    p.add_argument("--thanks", action="store_true")
    return p


def _apply_fixes(records, mode):
    if mode not in ("unsafe-only", "all"):
        return []
    changed = []
    for record in records:
        path = record["path"]
        if path == "<stdin>":
            continue
        lines = record["content"].splitlines(keepends=True)
        edits = 0
        for i, line in enumerate(list(lines)):
            match = re.match(r'^(\s*)-\s+uses:\s*["\']?actions/checkout@[^\s"\']+', line)
            if not match:
                continue
            indent = len(match.group(1))
            end = next((j for j in range(i + 1, len(lines))
                        if lines[j].strip() and len(lines[j]) - len(lines[j].lstrip()) <= indent), len(lines))
            block = "".join(lines[i:end])
            if re.search(r'^\s+persist-credentials:\s*false\b', block, re.M):
                continue
            with_line = next((j for j in range(i + 1, end)
                              if re.match(r'^\s{'+str(indent+2)+r'}with\s*:', lines[j])), None)
            if with_line is None:
                eol = "\r\n" if line.endswith("\r\n") else "\n"
                lines[i+1:i+1] = [" "*(indent+2)+"with:"+eol, " "*(indent+4)+"persist-credentials: false"+eol]
            else:
                eol = "\r\n" if lines[with_line].endswith("\r\n") else "\n"
                lines.insert(with_line+1, " "*(indent+4)+"persist-credentials: false"+eol)
            edits += 1
        if edits:
            updated = "".join(lines)
            try:
                with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as stream:
                    stream.write(updated)
                changed.append((path, edits))
            except OSError:
                continue
    return changed


def main(argv=None):
    argv = list(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv)
    if handle_special(argv):
        return 0
    args = parser().parse_args(argv)
    if args.fix and "-" in args.inputs:
        sys.stderr.write("error: `--fix` cannot be used with `-` (stdin)\n\nUsage: zizmor [OPTIONS] <INPUT>...\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
        return 2
    if args.thanks:
        print("zizmor's development is sustained by our generous sponsors:\n🌈 Grafana Labs\n🌈 Kusari")
        return 0
    if args.completions:
        completion_path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "completions", args.completions)
        try:
            with open(completion_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
                sys.stdout.write(stream.read())
        except OSError:
            pass
        return 0
    if args.lsp:
        return 0
    if not args.inputs:
        sys.stderr.write("error: the following required arguments were not provided:\n  <INPUT>...\n\nUsage: executable <INPUT>...\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
        return 2
    kinds=[]
    for group in args.collect:
        kinds.extend(x.strip() for x in group.split(",") if x.strip())
    kinds=kinds or ["default"]
    if "workflows-only" in kinds: kinds=["workflows" if x=="workflows-only" else x for x in kinds]
    if "actions-only" in kinds: kinds=["actions" if x=="actions-only" else x for x in kinds]
    if not set(kinds) <= {"all","default","workflows","actions","dependabot"}:
        sys.stderr.write("error: invalid value for '--collect <KIND>...'\n")
        return 2
    try:
        inputs=collect(args.inputs, collect=kinds)
    except ValueError as e:
        sys.stderr.write(f"error: {e}\n")
        return 2
    if not inputs:
        # Distinguish missing local paths from valid repositories that produced no files.
        for item in args.inputs:
            if item != "-" and not os.path.exists(item) and not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+(?:@[^/]+)?", item):
                sys.stderr.write(f"fatal: no audit was performed\ninvalid input: {item}\n")
                return 1
        sys.stderr.write("fatal: no audit was performed\nno inputs collected\n")
        return 3
    applied_fixes = _apply_fixes(inputs, args.fix)
    findings=[]
    persona="Pedantic" if args.pedantic else args.persona.capitalize()
    for record in inputs:
        path, content=record["path"], record["content"]
        if not content.strip() or not re.search(r'(?m)^\s*(on|jobs|name|runs|version|updates|package-ecosystem)\s*:',content):
            sys.stderr.write(f"fatal: no audit was performed\nfailed to load {path} as {record['kind'][:-1] if record['kind'].endswith('s') else record['kind']}\n")
            return 3
        if re.search(r'(?m)^\s*:\s*[^\n]*$',content):
            sys.stderr.write(f"fatal: no audit was performed\nfailed to load {path} as {record['kind']}\n")
            return 1
        current = audit_text(content,path,pedantic=(persona == "Pedantic"))
        if args.pedantic or args.persona in ("pedantic", "auditor"):
            current.extend(concurrency_findings(content, path))
            current.extend(pedantic_permission_findings(content, path))
        if args.persona == "auditor" and not args.pedantic:
            current.extend(auditor_findings(content, path))
            # Auditor mode includes findings admitted by the pedantic persona too.
            seen = {(f.get("ident"), repr(f.get("locations"))) for f in current}
            for extra in audit_text(content, path, pedantic=True):
                key = (extra.get("ident"), repr(extra.get("locations")))
                if key not in seen:
                    extra["determinations"]["persona"] = "Pedantic"
                    current.append(extra)
                    seen.add(key)
        cfg = discover_config(path, args.config, args.no_config)
        current = apply_config(current, cfg, path, args.no_ignores)
        if not args.no_ignores:
            current = filter_inline_ignores(current, content)
        findings.extend(current)
    persona="Pedantic" if args.pedantic else args.persona.capitalize()
    if args.persona == "regular" and not args.pedantic:
        findings=[f for f in findings if f["ident"] != "anonymous-definition"]
    if args.persona != "auditor" or args.pedantic:
        for finding in findings:
            is_regular_permissions = ((args.pedantic or args.persona == "pedantic")
                and finding.get("ident") == "excessive-permissions"
                and len(finding.get("locations", [])) > 1
                and finding["locations"][0].get("symbolic", {}).get("route", {}).get("route", [])[:1] == [{"Key": "jobs"}])
            finding["determinations"]["persona"] = "Regular" if is_regular_permissions else persona
    sev_order={"informational":0,"low":1,"medium":2,"high":3}
    conf_order={"low":1,"medium":2,"high":3}
    if args.min_severity:
        findings=[f for f in findings if sev_order.get(f["determinations"]["severity"].lower(),1)>=sev_order[args.min_severity]]
    if args.min_confidence:
        findings=[f for f in findings if conf_order.get(f["determinations"]["confidence"].lower(),1)>=conf_order[args.min_confidence]]
    rule_order = {name: i for i, name in enumerate(("artipacked", "excessive-permissions", "dangerous-triggers", "template-injection", "unpinned-uses", "unpinned-images", "insecure-commands", "secrets-inherit", "concurrency-limits", "anonymous-definition", "self-hosted-runner"))}
    persona_order = {"Pedantic": 0, "Auditor": 1, "Regular": 2}
    findings.sort(key=lambda f: (rule_order.get(f.get("ident", ""), 100),
                                 persona_order.get(f.get("determinations", {}).get("persona", "Regular"), 3)))
    rendered = render(findings,args.format)
    if applied_fixes:
        rendered += "\nFix Summary\nSuccessfully applied fixes to {} files:\n".format(len(applied_fixes))
        rendered += "".join("  {}: {} fixes\n".format(path, count) for path, count in applied_fixes)
    sys.stdout.write(rendered)
    if findings and not args.no_exit_codes and args.format != "sarif":
        return 14 if any(f.get("determinations", {}).get("severity") == "High" for f in findings) else 13
    return 0

if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

"""Output formatters for audit finding records."""
import json
import re

VERSION = "1.25.2"
SCHEMA = "https://docs.oasis-open.org/sarif/sarif/v2.1.0/os/schemas/sarif-schema-2.1.0.json"


def _level(f):
    return f.get("determinations", {}).get("severity", "Low")


def _place(f):
    locs = f.get("locations", [])
    if not locs:
        return "<stdin>", 1
    x = locs[0].get("concrete", {}).get("location", {}).get("start_point", {})
    line = x.get("row", 0) + 1
    sym = locs[0].get("symbolic", {}).get("key", {})
    path = sym.get("Local", {}).get("given_path", "<stdin>")
    return path, line


def _github(f):
    path, line = _place(f)
    level = "error" if _level(f) == "High" else "warning"
    annotation = ""
    loc = (f.get("locations") or [{}])[0]
    annotation = loc.get("symbolic", {}).get("annotation", "")
    desc = f.get("desc", "")
    msg = f"{path}:{line}: {desc}: {annotation}".replace("%", "%25").replace("\r", "%0D").replace("\n", "%0A")
    return f"::{level} file={path},line={line},title={f.get('ident','')}::{msg}"


def _sarif(findings):
    rules = []
    seen = set()
    results = []
    for f in findings:
        ident = f.get("ident", "unknown")
        uri = f.get("url", f"https://docs.zizmor.sh/audits/#{ident}")
        if ident not in seen:
            seen.add(ident)
            rules.append({"id": f"zizmor/{ident}", "name": ident, "shortDescription": {"text": f.get("desc", "")}, "helpUri": uri, "properties": {"tags": ["security"]}})
        path, line = _place(f)
        annotation = ((f.get("locations") or [{}])[0].get("symbolic", {}).get("annotation", ""))
        severity = _level(f)
        results.append({"ruleId": f"zizmor/{ident}", "level": "error" if severity == "High" else "warning", "kind": "fail", "message": {"text": f.get("desc", "") + (": " + annotation if annotation else "")}, "locations": [{"physicalLocation": {"artifactLocation": {"uri": path}, "region": {"startLine": line, "startColumn": 1}}}], "properties": {"zizmor/severity": severity, "zizmor/confidence": f.get("determinations", {}).get("confidence", "Low"), "zizmor/persona": f.get("determinations", {}).get("persona", "Regular")}})
    driver = {"name": "zizmor", "version": VERSION, "semanticVersion": VERSION,
              "informationUri": "https://docs.zizmor.sh", "downloadUri": "https://github.com/zizmorcore/zizmor", "rules": rules}
    run = {"invocations": [{"executionSuccessful": True}], "results": results, "tool": {"driver": driver}}
    return {"$schema": SCHEMA, "runs": [run], "version": "2.1.0"}


def render(findings, fmt="plain"):
    if fmt in ("json", "json-v1"):
        return json.dumps(findings, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n"
    if fmt == "github":
        return "".join(_github(f) + "\n" for f in findings)
    if fmt == "sarif":
        return json.dumps(_sarif(findings), ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n"
    if not findings:
        return "No findings to report. Good job!\n"
    chunks = []
    for f in findings:
        path, line = _place(f)
        level = _level(f).lower()
        annotation = (f.get("locations") or [{}])[0].get("symbolic", {}).get("annotation", "")
        chunks.append(f"{level}[{f.get('ident','unknown')}]: {f.get('desc','')}\n --> {path}:{line}:1\n  = note: {annotation}\n  = help: audit documentation → {f.get('url','')}\n")
    return "\n".join(chunks)
# this disables all online actions, including repository fetches
zizmor --offline workflow.yml

# passing a token explicitly will enable online mode
# in this case, we use the `gh` CLI token
zizmor --gh-token $(gh auth token) workflow.yml

# online for the purpose of fetching the input (example/example),
# but all audits themselves are offline
zizmor --no-online-audits --gh-token $(gh auth token) example/example
```

### GitHub API token permissions

!!! tip

    If you're running `zizmor` locally with an online mode, it is
    **strongly recommended** that you use `gh auth token` from the [GitHub CLI]
    to automatically access an API token and avoid error-prone manual
    provisioning.

    This token is almost always pre-configured with sufficient permissions,
    meaning that you **do not** need any of the manual steps below.

    [GitHub CLI]: https://cli.github.com/

When running in an online mode, `zizmor` uses the GitHub API for
various operations, including fetching a repository's contents
(for the collection phase) and fetching tag/branch/commit histories
(for the auditing phase).

Generally speaking, `zizmor` does **not** require any special permissions
from its GitHub API token: it uses the token *primarily* to provide
authentication for rate-limited API requests.

However, if you are auditing a private remote repository (e.g.
`zizmor myorg/private-repo`) or auditing _any_ input that contains
private references (e.g. `#!yaml uses: myorg/private-action`), then
you may need to provision permissions for the token:

- `#!yaml contents: read` for GitHub Actions
- `repo` for OAuth tokens and "classic" PATs
- An appropriate repository access scope for fine-grained PATs

In addition to these permissions, some integrations of `zizmor`
(like GitHub Advanced Security) may require additional permissions
in the context of GitHub Actions. See
[Integration - GitHub Actions](./integrations.md#github-actions) for more details.

## Output formats

`zizmor` always produces output on `stdout`.

### Cargo-style output ("plain")

By default, `zizmor` produces `cargo`-style diagnostic output.

```console
error[template-injection]: code injection via template expansion
  --> ./tests/integration/test-data/template-injection/pr-425-backstop/action.yml:31:56
   |
29 |       uses: azure/powershell@whatever
   |       ------------------------------- action accepts arbitrary code
30 |       with:
31 |         inlineScript: Get-AzVM -ResourceGroupName "${{ inputs.expandme }}"
   |         ------------ via this input                    ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ may expand into attacker-controllable code
   |
   = note: audit confidence → High
```

This output will be colorized by default when sent to a supporting terminal and
uncolorized by default when piped to another program. Users can also explicitly
disable output colorization by setting `NO_COLOR=1` in their environment.

This format can also be explicitly selected with `--format=plain`.

#### Audit documentation links

By default, `zizmor` includes links to relevant documentation pages
for each finding in its plain output format. These links are provided via
[OSC 8](https://gist.github.com/egmontkob/eb114294efbcd5adb1944c9f3cb5feda)
hyperlinks, which are supported by many modern terminal emulators.

For example, in the output above, `template-injection` within
`error[template-injection]: ...` is a clickable link that takes you to
the [template-injection](./audits#template-injection) audit documentation.

In addition to these OSC 8 links, `zizmor` also includes the full URL
as part of each finding _if_ it detects a non-terminal output _or_
a CI environment (e.g. GitHub Actions).

        start = span.get("start_point", {})
        end = span.get("end_point", {})
        start_row = start.get("row", line - 1)
        start_col = start.get("column", column - 1)
        end_row = end.get("row", start_row)
        end_col = end.get("column", start_col)
        source = source_map.get(path, "")
        raw = source.encode("utf-8")
        offsets = span.get("offset_span", {})
        begin = offsets.get("start", 0)
        finish = offsets.get("end", begin)
        snippet = raw[begin:finish].decode("utf-8", errors="replace") if source else concrete.get("feature", "")
        if source and finish < len(raw) and raw[finish:finish+1] == b"\\n":
            line_start = raw.rfind(b"\\n", 0, finish) + 1
            if finish == len(raw) or raw[finish:finish+1] == b"\\n":
                snippet += "\\n"
                end_row += 1
                end_col = 0
        region = {"startLine": start_row + 1, "startColumn": start_col + 1,
                  "endLine": end_row + 1, "endColumn": end_col + 1,
                  "snippet": {"text": snippet, "sourceLanguage": "yaml"}}
        results.append({"ruleId": f"zizmor/{ident}", "level": "error" if severity == "High" else "warning", "kind": "fail", "message": {"text": f.get("desc", "") + (": " + annotation if annotation else "")}, "locations": [{"physicalLocation": {"artifactLocation": {"uri": path}, "region": region}}], "properties": {"zizmor/severity": severity, "zizmor/confidence": f.get("determinations", {}).get("confidence", "Low"), "zizmor/persona": f.get("determinations", {}).get("persona", "Regular")}})

def _plain_location(location, path, source_map):
    concrete = location.get("concrete", {})
    loc = concrete.get("location", {})
    start = loc.get("start_point", {})
    end = loc.get("end_point", {})
    row = max(0, start.get("row", 0))
    col = max(0, start.get("column", 0))
    endrow = max(row, end.get("row", row))
    endcol = max(0, end.get("column", col))
    src = source_map.get(path, "").splitlines()
    if not src:
        src = [concrete.get("feature", "")]
    endrow = min(endrow, len(src) - 1)
    width = len(str(endrow + 1))
    lines = ["  |"]
    for n in range(row, endrow + 1):
        source = src[n] if n < len(src) else ""
        lines.append(f"{n+1:>{width}} | {source}")
        if n == row:
            span = max(1, endcol - col) if endrow == row else max(1, len(source) - col)
            gutter = f"  {' ':>{width}} | "
            annotation = location.get("symbolic", {}).get("annotation", "")
            lines.append(gutter + " " * col + "^" * span + (" " + annotation if annotation else ""))
    if endrow > row:
        lines.append(f"  {' ':>{width}} |{'_' * max(1, len(src[endrow]))}- " + location.get("symbolic", {}).get("annotation", ""))
    lines.append("  |")

"""Output formatters for audit finding records."""
import json
import re

VERSION = "1.25.2"
SCHEMA = "https://docs.oasis-open.org/sarif/sarif/v2.1.0/os/schemas/sarif-schema-2.1.0.json"


def _level(f):
    return f.get("determinations", {}).get("severity", "Low")


def _place(f):
    locs = f.get("locations", [])
    if not locs:
        return "<stdin>", 1, 1
    x = locs[0].get("concrete", {}).get("location", {}).get("start_point", {})
    line = x.get("row", 0) + 1
    sym = locs[0].get("symbolic", {}).get("key", {})
    path = sym.get("Local", {}).get("given_path", "<stdin>")
    return path, line, x.get("column", 0) + 1


def _github(f):
    path, line, _ = _place(f)
    level = "error" if _level(f) == "High" else "warning"
    annotation = ""
    loc = (f.get("locations") or [{}])[0]
    annotation = loc.get("symbolic", {}).get("annotation", "")
    desc = f.get("desc", "")
    msg = f"{path}:{line}: {desc}: {annotation}".replace("%", "%25").replace("\r", "%0D").replace("\n", "%0A")
    return f"::{level} file={path},line={line},title={f.get('ident','')}::{msg}"


def _sarif(findings, source_map=None):
    source_map = source_map or {}
    rules = []
    seen = set()
    results = []
    for f in findings:
        ident = f.get("ident", "unknown")
        uri = f.get("url", f"https://docs.zizmor.sh/audits/#{ident}")
        if ident not in seen:
            seen.add(ident)
            rules.append({"id": f"zizmor/{ident}", "name": ident, "shortDescription": {"text": f.get("desc", "")}, "helpUri": uri, "properties": {"tags": ["security"]}})
        path, line, column = _place(f)
        annotation = ((f.get("locations") or [{}])[0].get("symbolic", {}).get("annotation", ""))
        severity = _level(f)
        first_loc = (f.get("locations") or [{}])[0]
        concrete = first_loc.get("concrete", {})
        span = concrete.get("location", {})
        start = span.get("start_point", {})
        end = span.get("end_point", {})
        start_row = start.get("row", line - 1)
        start_col = start.get("column", column - 1)
        end_row = end.get("row", start_row)
        end_col = end.get("column", start_col)
        source = source_map.get(path, "")
        raw = source.encode("utf-8")
        offsets = span.get("offset_span", {})
        begin = offsets.get("start", 0)
        finish = offsets.get("end", begin)
        snippet = raw[begin:finish].decode("utf-8", errors="replace") if source else concrete.get("feature", "")
        if (source and finish < len(raw) and raw[finish:finish+1] == b"\n"
                and (end_row > start_row or ident == "artipacked")):
            snippet += "\n"
            end_row += 1
            end_col = 0
        region = {"startLine": start_row + 1, "startColumn": start_col + 1,
                  "endLine": end_row + 1, "endColumn": end_col + 1,
                  "snippet": {"text": snippet}, "sourceLanguage": "yaml"}
        results.append({"ruleId": f"zizmor/{ident}", "level": "error" if severity == "High" else "warning", "kind": "fail", "message": {"text": f.get("desc", "") + (": " + annotation if annotation else "")}, "locations": [{"physicalLocation": {"artifactLocation": {"uri": path}, "region": region}}], "properties": {"zizmor/severity": severity, "zizmor/confidence": f.get("determinations", {}).get("confidence", "Low"), "zizmor/persona": f.get("determinations", {}).get("persona", "Regular")}})
    driver = {"name": "zizmor", "version": VERSION, "semanticVersion": VERSION,
              "informationUri": "https://docs.zizmor.sh", "downloadUri": "https://github.com/zizmorcore/zizmor", "rules": rules}
    run = {"invocations": [{"executionSuccessful": True}], "results": results, "tool": {"driver": driver}}
    return {"$schema": SCHEMA, "runs": [run], "version": "2.1.0"}


def _plain_location(location, path, source_map):
    concrete = location.get("concrete", {})
    loc = concrete.get("location", {})
    start = loc.get("start_point", {})
    end = loc.get("end_point", {})
    row = max(0, start.get("row", 0))
    col = max(0, start.get("column", 0))
    endrow = max(row, end.get("row", row))
    endcol = max(0, end.get("column", col))
    src = source_map.get(path, "").splitlines()
    if not src:
        src = [concrete.get("feature", "")]
    endrow = min(endrow, len(src) - 1)
    width = len(str(endrow + 1))
    lines = ["  |"]
    for n in range(row, endrow + 1):
        source = src[n] if n < len(src) else ""
        lines.append(f"{n+1:>{width}} | {source}")
        if n == row:
            span = max(1, endcol - col) if endrow == row else max(1, len(source) - col)
            gutter = f"  {' ':>{width}} | "
            annotation = location.get("symbolic", {}).get("annotation", "")
            lines.append(gutter + " " * col + "^" * span + (" " + annotation if annotation else ""))
    if endrow > row:
        lines.append(f"  {' ':>{width}} |{'_' * max(1, len(src[endrow]))}- " + location.get("symbolic", {}).get("annotation", ""))
    lines.append("  |")
    return lines


def _plain(findings, source_map, suppressed=0):
    if not findings:
        suffix = f" ({suppressed} suppressed)" if suppressed else ""
        return f"No findings to report. Good job!{suffix}\n"
    chunks = []
    counts = {"informational": 0, "low": 0, "medium": 0, "high": 0}
    for f in findings:
        severity = _level(f).lower()
        counts[severity] = counts.get(severity, 0) + 1
        level = "error" if severity == "high" else "warning"
        locs = f.get("locations", [])
        path, line, col = _place(f)
        chunks.append(f"{level}[{f.get('ident','unknown')}]: {f.get('desc','')}\n --> {path}:{line}:{col}")
        for location in locs[:2]:
            chunks.extend(_plain_location(location, path, source_map))
        confidence = f.get("determinations", {}).get("confidence", "Low")
        chunks.append(f"  = note: audit confidence → {confidence}")
        if f.get("ident") == "artipacked":
            chunks.append("  = note: this finding has an auto-fix")
        chunks.append(f"  = help: audit documentation → {f.get('url','')}")
        chunks.append("")
    summary = "{} findings: {} informational, {} low, {} medium, {} high".format(
        len(findings), counts["informational"], counts["low"], counts["medium"], counts["high"])
    if suppressed:
        summary = summary.replace(" findings:", f" findings ({suppressed} suppressed):")
    chunks.append(summary)
    return "\n".join(chunks) + "\n"


def render(findings, fmt="plain", source_map=None, suppressed=0):
    source_map = source_map or {}
    if fmt in ("json", "json-v1"):
        return json.dumps(findings, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n"
    if fmt == "github":
        return "".join(_github(f) + "\n" for f in findings)
    if fmt == "sarif":
        return json.dumps(_sarif(findings, source_map), ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n"
    return _plain(findings, source_map, suppressed)
